newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour says Bolger comments "economic sabotage".
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour says Bolger comments "economic sabotage".

text.p: New Zealand's opposition Labour Party accused Prime Minister Jim Bolger of economic sabotage on Monday after he encouraged overseas investors to take a "wait and see" approach until the October 12 election.
Bolger was asked in an Australian television interview on Sunday what assurances he could offer investors who were worried by political uncertainty.
"I can only say that their uncertainty or their question mark at this stage two weeks out is totally understandable," Bolger said.

"If I was an Australian investor, I would just wait two weeks as well, or as an overseas investor, and then if a sensible coalition forms, well obviously we are going to continue with a strong economy that we've got, and therefore we would welcome the investors to come in and make the investment decisions they wish to," Bolger said.
Labour leader Helen Clark said Bolger was seeking to "drag down the New Zealand economy as he faces defeat" in the election.
"What could be more irresponsible than to warn foreign investors not to invest in New Zealand before the general election?" Clark said in a statement.

She said the inference from Bolger's message to foreign investors was not only that they should not invest in New Zealand before the election, but also that they should not invest if there was a change of government.

"Mr Bolger's message is no less than economic sabotage of his country ... what appals me is that Mr Bolger has cynically set out to destroy the New Zealand economy because the people of New Zealand are likely to judge him no longer fit to govern."

Bolger's National Party has been campaigning on the promise of economic stability, telling voters the alternative is a "three-headed monster" of Labour, economic nationalist New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance.
The three parties, according to latest opinion polls, may be on course to win a majority of seats in parliament, but their coalition prospects remain unclear.

"I don't think anybody will be wanting to invest in New Zealand if (Alliance leader) Jim Anderton's economic policies were to be at the forefront of any coalition government in the future," Bolger said in the interview.
"That's the sort of risk we've got on one side, and that's why I imagine investors are holding back."
"Let me say to Australians, if we get some of the loopy policies of the left come in to New Zealand again, you will get a whole lot of Kiwis over there in a hurry," he said.
Clark said the suggestion of an exodus of New Zealanders to Austrlia was "outrageous".

She added: "There is every prospect now that Labour will lead the next government. Labour has responsible and orthodox economic policies designed to promote both price stability and economic growth. "This economy requires the confidence of foreign investors and Labour will maintain that confidence." -- Wellington newsroon 64 4 4734746
